candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the applicable limit is compared against a geometric mean versus another aggregation (or a single measurement) changes which reported values are used and whether a measurement exceeds the limit.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Substituting one-half the detection limit for a nondetect can change the effluent concentration used in limit derivation and compliance comparison; it also distinguishes a computed surrogate value from a true no-data state for missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating the result as no data removes it from limit calculations and compliance comparisons, and establishes a documented no-data state rather than a numeric surrogate or violation.

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The permissive choice between the reported below-MQL value and zero changes the effluent term in concentration calculations and limit comparisons; it also affects whether missing-evidence is classified as a usable numeric input versus an unresolved substitution.

This formula defines how effluent and ambient inputs translate into an instream waste concentration; different readings of its terms or the 2.13 factor change the derived limit against which measurements are compared.

candidates.exact_span: F = Fraction of stream allow ed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F directly scales ambient and effluent contributions in Cd; a different authorized mixing fraction yields a different applicable instream limit.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selecting 4Q3 versus harmonic mean flow changes Qa in the Cd calculation and thus the applicable limit; it also bears on which flow statistic must be available (and potentially monitored or documented) to establish the correct limit.

This conversion from total to dissolved metal fraction determines the dissolved criteria derived from total metal criteria; different interpretation of Kp or TSS inputs changes the enforceable dissolved limit.

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TSS is taken from the receiving stream or from effluent for an intermittent stream changes Kp, C/Ct, and the resulting dissolved metal limit; it also affects which TSS evidence must exist to support the limit calculation.

candidates.exact_span: Stream Linear Partition Coefficient                                                             Lake Linear Partition Coefficient
candidates.computation_change_reason: The segment presents parallel stream and lake coefficient sets with different Kpo, alpha, Kp, C/Ct, and dissolved values; which column applies changes the derived dissolved metal limit for a given total metal criterion.

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 750 in cell O113
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional overrides the hardness-derived acute aluminum criterion; whether pH is below 6.5 changes the applicable acute limit and implicates whether pH monitoring or documentation was required to determine applicability.

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 87 in cell P113
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional overrides the hardness-derived chronic aluminum criterion; whether pH is below 6.5 changes the applicable chronic limit and implicates whether pH evidence was needed to establish which criterion applies.

The cadmium acute correction factor depends on hardness; different hardness values or interpretations change the acute dissolved cadmium limit and whether hardness monitoring was required to establish it.
